351.intention: A shared-anchor expert pair, not a new-rule demonstration: Blue reaches the right anchor, while Coral moves to the left boundary to stop Blue on its downward nest column. Coral then comes up against a rock, circles right and reuses the same anchor to stop against Blue in its own upward capture column. Blue must finish downward before Coral goes up and left home. Removed the second anchor masked by the adjacent rock; the two physical helper launches and thirteen-input optimum remain.

352.intention: Blue drops while Coral loops down and left to become Blue's bottom-row wall. The Heart-only gate then rejects Blue upward, giving Blue the row to travel right and become Coral's upper wall. Coral relocates through the lower rocks and stops against Blue; Blue returns left, down and left home before Coral captures left on its own row. The same gate permits Coral in reachable alternatives but stops Blue in the actual solution. Removed the unused Spade gate rather than claiming another permission interaction.

353.intention: Coral initially stops Blue's lower-left and downward approaches. Blue parks on the left boundary so Coral can loop right, up and left against it while passing its own Coral gate. Coral then moves upward; the same Coral-only gate rejects Blue rightward and fixes Blue's upward capture column. Release Coral for its rightward nest only after Blue captures. Removed the unused Blue gate: one color permission already serves both the allowed traveler and the rejected traveler in the reciprocal setup.

354.intention: Two directional rejections build a reciprocal launch: the upper rail stops Coral leftward, allowing Blue to loop around the lower-right rock and stop below Coral. Coral's downward input is then rejected by the upward rail and it moves left against Blue. After Coral relocates along the lower-left column, it stops Blue in its final downward capture column; Coral captures left last. The upward rail also permits Blue's earlier upward passage, so the directions do different physical jobs.

355.intention: Coral first vacates the left column to the bottom. Blue moves left, up and right to stop Coral's return across the upper row, then loops up and left. Coral moves upward to stop Blue immediately above the remaining counterclockwise turner; Blue's downward input visibly bends right into its nest. Coral captures left afterward. Removed the first corner turner, whose boundary/rock stop did not contribute a useful bend or change the independent twelve-input optimum.

356.intention: A seventeen-input state/cooperation pair: Blue first uses Coral at the right edge, then returns downward to stop Coral in the switch column. Coral uses the still-closed upper door to stop on the switch row, crosses the switch rightward, goes up and left through the opened door, and returns down to become Blue's final wall. Blue captures upward; Coral returns through the persistent open route, goes down through its own switch again, and captures left. The state and relocated helper loop are connected, not isolated toggles.

357.intention: Blue uses the lower anchor and side rocks to reach the upper-left helper position. Coral approaches upward against Blue; Blue then moves right and down onto the central anchor. Coral relocates right and upward to become Blue's upper stopper, allowing Blue to move up and left home. Coral captures left only after Blue leaves. Both precise launch points feed the changing helper roles; neither is a straight continuation tax.

358.intention: Keep exchanging roles before releasing either resident: Coral at the upper-right first stops Blue after Blue's permitted Spade-gate passage. The Heart-only gate rejects Blue leftward for its next approach. Blue and Coral then exchange upper-row stopping positions before Blue drops and circles left; Coral drops to the rock row and stops Blue in its final downward nest column. Blue captures down, then Coral captures left. Both gates have actual identity-dependent work, and four helper jobs occur before the first release.

359.intention: The Coral-only upper gate rejects Blue, placing it where it stops Coral from below. Coral moves to the right edge while Blue circles along the bottom and passes its own Blue gate upward against Coral. Blue captures downward from the adjacent rock's column. The Blue-only gate now rejects Coral's downward approach, giving Coral the row to move left and then upward home. The residents need opposite permissions at different stages, not matching colored scenery.

360.intention: Coral first passes the left-entry rail toward the left edge, then tries the reverse entry and stops short of that same tile. This rejection gives Coral the column to move upward against Blue. After Coral circles to the right, it stops Blue downward; Coral then returns upward until the top right-entry rail rejects it, preparing Blue's rightward stop and upward capture. Release Coral leftward last. The first rail has both actual allowed and rejected entries in the intended solution, and three helper jobs connect the two residents. This thirteen-input replacement supersedes the rejected universal-arrow-wall proposal.

361.intention: Coral waits on the lower anchor while Mint uses Blue at the top-right. Mint descends and then visibly bends upward at the clockwise turner; its new top position stops Blue beside its nest column. Mint next descends through the same turner, bends left, and drops to the bottom to stop Coral as it leaves the anchor. Coral's upward input bends right at the turner, then its next upward move stops below Blue. Coral captures left before Blue captures down; Mint loops around the lower-left edge and captures upward last. Four physical helper jobs connect the shared turner and timed anchor departure. This fourteen-input design replaces the earlier cosmetic-rail proposal.

362.intention: Blue reaches the bottom-right approach and travels up through the permitted Spade gate and upward rail to become Mint's rightward wall. Mint relocates upward and stops Coral's approach; Coral then becomes Blue's leftward wall after the rail rejects Blue downward. Blue captures down, while the same Spade gate rejects Coral rightward onto its downward nest column. Coral captures next, freeing Mint's downward capture last. The rail and suit gate each have actual permitted and rejected uses; the bottom anchor was physically redundant with the boundary and was removed.

363.intention: Mint first uses Coral at the right side, then travels up and left against Blue at the top-left. The Blue-only gate rejects Mint downward, preparing Mint's relocation to the upper-right helper position. Meanwhile Coral's downward input visibly bends left at the clockwise bottom turner to become Blue's lower wall. Blue uses Mint to align its column, then Coral to align its leftward bottom capture. Coral captures upward next and Mint captures left after returning down around the rocks. Four physical helper jobs connect the color restriction and turn; the unused anchor was removed with the sixteen-input optimum intact.

Mint descends through the permitted downward rail and open door against Coral, moves right against Blue and drops. Blue returns left and upward until the same rail rejects its reverse entry; Coral rises against Blue. Blue captures right, Coral right, and Mint left. The linked passage, two-direction rail and four helper jobs form one relay. The unvisited anchor was removed without changing the twelve-input optimum.

The shared anchor, identity distinction and three physical helper jobs all matter; the unused Blue gate was removed with the fifteen-input optimum intact.

The same Spade gate rejects Coral's rightward approach; Blue returns upward to stop Coral in Coral's downward capture column. Capture Coral, then Mint upward, then Blue downward through the cleared column. Suit contrast, directional rail and three physical helper jobs now make a genuine fourteen-input synthesis. Removed the masked/turnaround anchor and unused corner turner.

Blue travels right, bends downward onto its permitted color tile and captures left. Coral captures upward before Mint leaves its blocking position. The sixteen-input route connects opposing color permission, a real continuous turn and three-way cooperation. Blue rises through a clockwise bend, travels right through the open door and stops against Coral. Blue captures down, Coral captures left through the door, and Mint captures left last. The thirteen-input route connects a physical helper-to-turn launch, persistent state and the final helper endpoint.
